subject: Literature
title: Mesoamerican Origin Stories
description: A 60-second lesson on Mesoamerican Origin Stories.

hook.text: The Mayan Popol Vuh tells of gods who created humans from corn after their earlier creations kept failing.

buildup.text: The gods first tried mud and wood, but those humans lacked souls, so the gods destroyed them and tried again.

discovery.text: The Popol Vuh was preserved by a Mayan scribe who secretly transcribed it after the Spanish conquest.

twist.text: Spanish colonizers burned nearly all Mayan books, making this secretly saved text one of very few survivors.

climax.text: The Popol Vuh preserves a complete worldview that would have been lost forever without one act of defiance.

punchline.text: One scribe saved an entire civilization's story.

quiz.question: How was the Popol Vuh preserved?
options: It was carved into a pyramid
A Mayan scribe secretly transcribed it after the Spanish conquest
Spanish missionaries translated and published it
